title: Caesarea Philippi + the Unnamed Mountain
subtitle: Northern ministry geography and the Transfiguration problem
summary: Explore the securely identified Paneas/Caesarea Philippi district alongside the Gospel’s unnamed Transfiguration mountain, preserving Tabor tradition and Hermon proposals without choosing a winner.
disclaimer: Paneas/Caesarea Philippi is securely located. The Transfiguration mountain is not named in the Gospels. Cameras for Tabor and Hermon show the physical mountains only in relation to their traditional/proposed identifications; they do not establish the Gospel mountain.

evidenceLegend.label: Established site
evidenceLegend.description: A securely identified ancient site or physical mountain represented by an existing atlas record.

evidenceLegend.label: Historical tradition
evidenceLegend.description: A long-lived commemorative identification that is not established by the Gospel text.

evidenceLegend.label: Modern proposal
evidenceLegend.description: A geographic proposal based on narrative sequence or physical geography rather than direct identification.

evidenceLegend.label: Unnamed / unresolved
evidenceLegend.description: The biblical text does not provide enough information for a secure coordinate.

entryCamera.note: Centers on the securely identified Paneas/Banias site; it does not imply that the Transfiguration occurred here.

comparison.label: Northern ministry geography
comparison.intro: Separate what the Gospels actually name from later tradition and modern geographic proposals.

options.label: Caesarea Philippi district
options.summary: The Paneas/Banias sanctuary and settlement area is securely identified; Matthew and Mark place Peter’s confession in the Caesarea Philippi district.
options.rationale: This is a firm geographic anchor for the northern sequence, though the exact conversational spot is not recoverable.
options.objections: A securely located district does not identify the later Transfiguration mountain.

camera.note: Camera centers on established Paneas/Banias as a regional anchor.

options.label: Unnamed high mountain
options.summary: The Synoptic Gospels describe a high mountain but do not name it.
options.rationale: The most evidence-aware visualization is to preserve the mountain as unlocated while comparing later identifications separately.
options.objections: Narrative proximity to Caesarea Philippi does not itself prove a particular summit.

camera.note: Broad northern-region framing only; this camera is explicitly not the location of the Transfiguration mountain.

options.label: Mount Tabor tradition
options.summary: Mount Tabor has a very old Christian Transfiguration tradition.
options.rationale: The tradition is historically important and should be visible as tradition rather than silently promoted to established geography.
options.objections: The Gospels do not name Tabor, and the narrative sequence does not establish this identification.

camera.note: Centers on physical Mount Tabor in its role as the traditional Transfiguration identification.

options.label: Mount Hermon proposal
options.summary: The Hermon massif is a common modern proposal because of elevation and proximity to the Caesarea Philippi episode.
options.rationale: It is a plausible geographic proposal worth comparing, not a secure identification.
options.objections: The Gospels do not name Hermon or provide enough information to establish the proposal.

camera.note: Centers on the physical Hermon massif only as a proposed Transfiguration region.

hotspots.label: Paneas / Caesarea Philippi
hotspots.summary: Securely identified sanctuary and settlement area anchoring the northern Gospel sequence.

whyShown.evidence: Paneas/Banias is securely identified and the Gospel text names the Caesarea Philippi district.
whyShown.inference: The conversation is not pinned to a particular shrine, cave, or building.
whyShown.alternatives: The district is an anchor for sequence, not proof of the next mountain location.

hotspots.label: Mount Tabor — traditional identification
hotspots.summary: Physical Mount Tabor shown in its later traditional role.

whyShown.evidence: Mount Tabor is a real, securely located mountain with a longstanding Christian tradition.
whyShown.inference: Its identification with the Gospel mountain is traditional, not established.
whyShown.alternatives: Hermon and other proposals remain possible; the Gospel mountain itself stays unpinned.

hotspots.label: Mount Hermon — modern proposal
hotspots.summary: Physical Hermon massif displayed as a possible geographic proposal, not as the Gospel mountain.

whyShown.evidence: Hermon is a real high massif near the northern ministry region.
whyShown.inference: Its Transfiguration identification is a modern geographic proposal.
whyShown.alternatives: Tabor tradition and an unresolved unnamed mountain remain distinct possibilities.
